goal.startingPoint: Ten weeks off with a stress reaction in the left shin. My physio cleared me to start walk-run.

promptHead: Athlete goal: return to running since Mon Sep 7 2026, 1 week in; the athlete says: Ten weeks off with a stress reaction in the left shin. My physio cleared me to start walk-run.

new.headline: Your first week back went cleanly: three walk-runs, all at 0/10 pain, with the shin quiet afterwards. Next week repeats that session twice, then steps up once on Saturday to 1.5 minute running pieces.

flags.title: Next-morning shin check
flags.detail: Check the left shin the morning after each run. Only take Saturday's step if Monday and Wednesday both stayed at 0/10 and the shin was quiet the next morning.

flags.title: Physio stop rule
flags.detail: If the shin aches during any run, stop running and walk home. Next time, repeat the previous session instead of adding to it.

flags.title: Pain-free weeks, 1 of 4
flags.detail: Keep every run easy, with no strides, hills or faster pieces, until you have four pain-free weeks in a row. Any pain, even pain that settles, restarts the count.

flags.title: Running pace
flags.detail: Keep the running pieces as relaxed as last week, around 6:45 to 6:50/km at effort 3/10. Right now the shin sets the pace, not your lungs.

flags.title: Goal timeline
flags.detail: Running 30 minutes non-stop by mid-October would mean building faster than is safe. Late December is more realistic.

new.analysis:
**Last week was what a first week back should look like.** All three walk-runs were at 0/10 pain and effort 3/10, and the shin stayed quiet afterwards. Your heart rate averaged 68 to 69 percent of your max, so this was gentle work for your heart and lungs.

| Session | Running pace | Avg HR | Effort | Pain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Sep 7 | 6:50/km | 121 | 3/10 | 0/10 |
| Wed Sep 9 | 6:45/km | 123 | 3/10 | 0/10 |
| Sat Sep 12 | 6:45/km | 122 | 3/10 | 0/10 |

**I count the minutes you spend running, not the length of the whole session.** Your splits show five rounds of about 1 minute running and 2 minutes walking each time. That makes 5 minutes of running per session and 15 minutes for the week. Running is what loads the shin, so that is the number the plan builds on.

**Next week adds about 7 percent, from 15 to 16 running minutes.** The only new thing is one session with longer running pieces, 1.5 minutes instead of 1. It goes on Saturday, after two days without running. Bone adapts more slowly than your heart and lungs, so your fitness will feel ready before your shin is.

**At a safe build, mid-October means running in short pieces, not 30 minutes non-stop.** With about 10 percent more running each week, mid-October works out to 20 to 23 running minutes a week. To run 30 minutes non-stop, you would need around 60 running minutes a week. That points to roughly late December, and your physio can confirm that timeline.

**The rest of your routine should stay the same.** Keep doing the calf and hip routine twice a week, and keep running on flat routes in the same shoes. Feeling nervous is normal. Each step is small enough that a bad day only means repeating a session, not losing ground.

safetyCallouts.title: Check in with your physio if the shin changes.
safetyCallouts.body: If it aches during a run, hurts when you walk, or aches at night, stop running and contact your physio before your next session.
